speaker: Elder Dale G. Renlund
title: “How Long Will It Be Ere They Believe Me?”
session: Saturday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

points.text: Elder Dale G. Renlund spoke about ““How Long Will It Be Ere They Believe Me?””.

quotes.text: In the late 1980s, Mr. Martin developed severe heart failure. Despite the most advanced medications available, his heart could not adequately support his circulation. He would die without a heart transplant. He became my team’s patient, and the wait for a donor heart began. His condition worsened, and mechanical pumps were implanted to sustain his life.
quotes.speaker: Elder Dale G. Renlund
quotes.talk: “How Long Will It Be Ere They Believe Me?”
quotes.session: Saturday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: We too can easily fall into the same trap that Mr. Martin did that morning in the hospital, especially when our day-to-day challenges loom. We focus on the here and now—the “cold oatmeal”—and lose sight of the bigger picture, both where we have been and God’s promises to us.
quotes.speaker: Elder Dale G. Renlund
quotes.talk: “How Long Will It Be Ere They Believe Me?”
quotes.session: Saturday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: This is not just a modern phenomenon. As recorded in the Old Testament, the Lord led the children of Israel out of slavery in Egypt. God saved them when they were trapped at the Red Sea and provided for them when they lacked food and water. Even when they complained about a monotonous diet, the Lord miraculously helped them. They survived because of God’s miracles, yet they repeatedly focused on cold oatmeal. As they overlooked both the Lord’s blessings and His promises, their trust eroded in God and in God’s prophet, Moses.
quotes.speaker: Elder Dale G. Renlund
quotes.talk: “How Long Will It Be Ere They Believe Me?”
quotes.session: Saturday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: When the children of Israel reached the promised land, they were intimidated by the challenges ahead. They again bemoaned their situation, saying, “Would God that we had died in the land of Egypt! or would God we had died in this wilderness!” In other words, they thought that they had it better before and that this challenge was surely too much, even for the Lord.
quotes.speaker: Elder Dale G. Renlund
quotes.talk: “How Long Will It Be Ere They Believe Me?”
quotes.session: Saturday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: Scripture records the Lord’s response: “And the Lord said unto Moses, … how long will it be ere they believe me, for all the signs which I have [shown] among them?” In other words, the Lord was asking: “Why don’t they trust me? Despite all I have done, why won’t they believe me?” How often the Lord reassured the children of Israel, and reassures us, of His constancy, declaring, “I will never break my covenant with you.”
quotes.speaker: Elder Dale G. Renlund
quotes.talk: “How Long Will It Be Ere They Believe Me?”
quotes.session: Saturday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: Perhaps you have been served more than your share of cold oatmeal. Perhaps, like the children of Israel, you have doubted God’s care for you, His willingness to succor you, or His capacity to keep His promises. Yet God invites us to trust Him and His promises.
quotes.speaker: Elder Dale G. Renlund
quotes.talk: “How Long Will It Be Ere They Believe Me?”
quotes.session: Saturday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: During His mortal ministry, the Savior told His disciples: “These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.” Jesus overcame the world; we do not have to do so ourselves. When our faith is centered on Jesus Christ, He promises spiritual peace no matter our circumstances. We can experience joy in our here and now because of Him and through our covenant relationship with Him.
quotes.speaker: Elder Dale G. Renlund
quotes.talk: “How Long Will It Be Ere They Believe Me?”
quotes.session: Saturday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: Faith in Jesus Christ frees us from uncertainty because our hope rests on His faithfulness and righteousness, not on our own. The prophet Lehi testified to his son Jacob, “Wherefore, I know that thou art redeemed, because of the righteousness of thy Redeemer.” Jacob was a good and faithful person. Yet his righteousness would not be the source of his redemption. No, Jacob’s redemption would come through the righteousness of Jesus Christ. The same is true for each of us.
